title: Keyboard Manager shortcut that uses WIN key breaks when enabling Grab And Move with modifier set to WIN key

judgment.rationale: The report gives a reproducible Win+Q to Alt+F4 failure when Grab And Move also uses Win. A second user reports that changing Grab And Move to Alt restores Win remappings, and the reporter now clarifies that the failure appears after reboot. This supports an interaction investigation, not a confirmed hook-ordering cause.
evidence: The reporter identifies PowerToys 0.101.2362 Stable from Microsoft Store and provides the Win+Q/Alt+F4 plus Grab And Move Win-modifier sequence.
The report says Windows Search opens and the remap only occasionally works after restarting the system.
A commenter reports that changing Grab And Move to Alt restores Win+foo remappings.
The latest reply says the failure occurs after reboot; no fix PR was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the post-reboot Win+Q sequence, compare Grab And Move set to Win versus Alt, and trace modifier event delivery before selecting a code correction.

fix_assessment.rationale: A coordinated keyboard-event correction may be applicable, but the exact loss or ordering of Win events is unverified. The possible duplicates are related symptoms rather than confirmed coverage of this module-interaction scenario.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Win modifier delivery across Grab And Move and Keyboard Manager
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Grab And Move may consume or replay Win modifier events while Keyboard Manager is tracking the same Win+Q chord, leaving the shortcut matcher with an incomplete or mistimed modifier state.
plan: Instrument the reported sequence to record Win keydown/keyup, Grab And Move hook disposition, replay decisions, and Keyboard Manager's observed modifier state.
Confirm hook ordering and whether the non-drag Win hold is passed through or replayed before the Win+Q action key is evaluated.
If event loss or reordering is confirmed, adjust the non-drag modifier path so the complete Win+Q sequence reaches Keyboard Manager exactly once without activating a drag.
Add regression coverage for Win+Q mapped to Alt+F4 with Grab And Move set to Win, including the no-mouse-action path and an actual drag path.
verification: Repeat the reporter's post-restart sequence and verify Win+Q consistently sends Alt+F4 without opening Windows Search.
Verify ordinary Win shortcuts still work when Grab And Move is configured with Win and that holding Win with a mouse action still activates Grab And Move.
Run the focused Grab And Move and Keyboard Manager hook/remapping tests.

confidence.rationale: The two modules have independent low-level keyboard handling paths and the observed Win event is unexpected, but no trace confirms event consumption or ordering as the failure mechanism.

issue_context.summary: Win+Q mapped to Alt+F4 becomes unreliable after reboot when Grab And Move uses Win; Windows Search may open. Switching Grab And Move to Alt reportedly restores Win remappings, but the event-level cause is unconfirmed.
known_information: The issue is open, labeled Issue-Bug and Product-Keyboard Manager, and has no assignee.
The reporter identifies PowerToys 0.101.2362 Stable and Microsoft Store installation.
The reported sequence is to map Win+Q to Alt+F4, set Grab And Move's modifier to Win, restart, then press Win+Q; Windows Search may open and repeated presses may eventually work.
Automated triage marked the reproduction steps sufficient and suggested #50906, #21319, #40012, and #47038 as possible related issues.
Current upstream code contains a Keyboard Manager shortcut-event path and a separate Grab And Move low-level keyboard hook.
A commenter confirms the Win+foo remapping problem and reports that switching Grab And Move's modifier to Alt fixes it.
The reporter latest reply clarifies that the failure appears after reboot.
inferences: The behavior may depend on how the two modules process Win events across reboot, but no trace confirms interception, replay, or ordering.
The Alt-modifier workaround supports a configuration interaction but does not identify the failing mechanism.
issue_context.analysis: The latest reply narrows the reproduction to the post-reboot state, but the mechanism remains unresolved. The report and workaround justify a targeted maintainer trace instead of another request for general logs.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and all three comments, including the post-reboot clarification.
Compared the issue-suggested reports #50906, #21319, #40012, and #47038; their triggers differ and none establishes the same configuration.
Prior focused source review identified separate Keyboard Manager shortcut processing and Grab And Move low-level keyboard handling; no current issue-linked fix PR was found.

actions.label: Trace Win shortcut with Grab And Move

reproduce.module: Keyboard Manager and Grab And Move
prerequisites: PowerToys 0.101.2362 Stable or a current build with both Keyboard Manager and Grab And Move available.
A test application in which Alt+F4 can close a window.
steps: In Keyboard Manager, map Win+Q to Alt+F4.
In Grab And Move, set the modifier key to Win and enable the module.
Restart PowerToys or Windows as in the report.
In a test application, press Win+Q several times without holding a mouse button; record whether Windows Search opens and whether the target window closes.
Change Grab And Move's modifier to Alt and repeat the same Win+Q sequence to compare with the reported workaround.
Repeat while tracing Win keydown/keyup and whether Grab And Move passes, swallows, or replays each event.
reproduce.expected_result: Win+Q consistently invokes the mapped Alt+F4 action without opening Windows Search, while Grab And Move remains available for its intended mouse interaction.
